meta.about: NATCO Pharma Limited (NATCO) is a vertically integrated, research and development focused pharmaceutical company engaged in developing, manufacturing, and marketing complex products for niche therapeutic areas. [1] NATCO has established its presence in all three business segments viz. finished dosage formulations (“FDF”), active pharmaceutical ingredients (“APIs”), Contract Manufacturing Business.[2]
meta.keyPoints: Business Segments[1] a) Pharmaceuticals (97% in FY26 vs 99% in FY25): i) Export Formulation: [2] [3] [4] The company manufactures and markets finished dosage formulations in 50+ countries, including the US, Canada, Brazil, and Europe, etc. It is ranked among the top 10 generic companies in sales in Canada. Its Major US partners include Sun Pharma, Alvogen, Teva, Mylan, Actavis, Lupin, Breckenridge Pharmaceuticals, and Dr. Reddy’s. Its international business focuses on Para IV filings, and it plans to expand into emerging markets like MENA, ASEAN, and LATAM.

profile.name: Natco Pharma Ltd
profile.text: Integrated, research-led generics company: export formulations (US via partners and its own front end, Canada, Brazil, MENA/Asia tenders), branded domestic formulations (oncology pioneer: Veenat generic imatinib, 2003), APIs and, since 2019, crop protection. Nine plants in India (seven pharma, two agro); two API and two formulation plants are USFDA-approved (Mekaguda, Chennai; Kothur, Visakhapatnam). 49% associate Adcock Ingram (South Africa).

guidance.text: FY27: revenue Rs3,400-3,500 cr, PAT Rs700-750 cr including the associate (at 35.75%); Adcock revenue US$580-600 mn and PAT US$47-48 mn; tax ~25%; R&D 7-9% of sales; Brazil to US$55-60 mn; Canada +10-15%; from FY28 'our earnings should compound around 15% to 25% every year'.

FY27 PAT 'around INR 750 crores. I am not changing the guidance'; 'gross sales will be between INR 3,300 crores to INR 3,400 crores'; Adcock 'normally... around INR 100 crores per quarter' of profit; capex Rs250-300 cr a year; two US launches with exclusivity in FY28; CHS breakeven for FY27; demerger may slip from December to about March.
FY26 revenue ~Rs4,300 cr and PAT Rs1,280-1,300 cr (actual: total revenue Rs4,376 cr, PAT Rs1,418.5 cr incl. the Rs115 cr tax credit).

grevlimid.text: In Dec-2015 Celgene (now BMS) settled the Revlimid (lenalidomide) patent case with Natco, its US partner Arrow International and Arrow's parent Watson (Actavis generics, now part of Teva): Natco got a volume-limited licence from Mar-2022 (expected to reach a mid-single-digit percentage of US capsules in the final year) and unlimited generic entry from 31-Jan-2026 (patents expire Apr-2027). Natco books a profit share on its partner's sales. Quotas reset each January and were sold early in the year: Q3FY25 and Q3FY26 export formulations fell to Rs286 cr and Rs421 cr ('We had 0 Revlimid this quarter', 12-Feb-2026). From Feb-2026 the product is a crowded generic: Q1FY27 lenalidomide was 'negligible'. Canada: Natco has the 'highest market share for Lenalidomide'.

pipeline.status: FTF; settled; sole exclusivity on the 10 mg strength, shared on 60 mg; launch date confidential, analysts cite CY2027; plant upgrade due by end-2026
Para-IV; tentative approval received; litigating patents running 7-8 years; trial 'in the next few months'; 180-day exclusivity in doubt because approval took over 30 months
Sole FTF; 'approved in 30 months' (29-May-2026); launch timing not disclosed
Sole FTF on certain strengths (partner Mylan/Viatris); Ozempic settled (date confidential), Wegovy not settled; no approval yet; answering FDA queries. Not filed in Canada or Brazil
Launched in the US in Mar-2026 with 4-5 generics sharing exclusivity: 'fairly competitive'

17 approvals (tentative or final) and 28 para-IVs; key para-IVs incl. apixaban, trifluridine/tipiracil, trabectedin, acalabrutinib, erdafitinib, rimegepant, cabazitaxel, capmatinib, risdiplam (31-Mar-2026); 8-10 ANDAs and 2-3 FTFs targeted a year

adcock.text: Natco Pharma South Africa acquired 34.88% of Adcock Ingram on 11-Nov-2025 (35.75% with existing stakes) for ZAR3,873 mn (Rs1,991.2 cr) plus Rs87.9 cr of costs, through a scheme that delisted Adcock from the JSE; Bidvest holds the rest. Goodwill ZAR1,182 mn (Rs649.4 cr) inside the Rs2,275.7 cr carrying value. July 2026: a further 13.25% for ZAR1.81 bn (~US$111 mn; ~Rs1,060 cr) took Natco to 49%; Bidvest keeps 51% and Natco has a right of first refusal. Equity-accounted; ~Rs10-15 cr a year of purchase-price amortisation. Adcock FY ending Jun-2026: revenue US$592 mn, PAT US$57 mn; FY24 US$531/45 mn, FY25 US$549/48 mn. Dividend received FY26 Rs36.9 cr. Natco filed three dossiers in South Africa; products expected ~2028.

chs.text: Crop Health Sciences (since 2019): CTPR (chlorantraniliprole) launched 2022 after patent litigation; 35 products, 8 CTPR-based (~30-35% of sales); fungicide Glanz (tebuconazole + trifloxystrobin) and cyantraniliprole (Cyanat, Q1FY26). Revenue Rs40.9 cr FY23, Rs108.3 cr FY24, Rs59.8 cr FY25, Rs138.2 cr FY26; Q1FY27 Rs40.8 cr with an EBITDA loss; breakeven targeted for FY27. Board-approved demerger into Natco Crop Health Sciences Ltd, pending regulatory approvals; timing slipped from Dec-2026 to ~Mar-2027 because of the fund-raise.

plants.text: Kothur (formulations): warning letter dated 8-Apr-2024 after an Oct-2023 inspection; reinspection Jun-2025; FDA close-out letter dated 25-Sep-2025. Mekaguda (API): inspected 2025, cleared (EIR). Chennai (API): inspected 2025, observations procedural, EIR received. Visakhapatnam (formulations): last inspected ~2.5-3 years ago, inspection expected in 2026.

innovation.text: Minority stakes: eGenesis (US$8 mn; gene-edited pig kidneys; FDA cleared a Phase 1/2/3 kidney study, 33-patient registration trial to start early 2027), Cellogen Therapeutics (CAR-T, India), Stero Therapeutics (US$1 mn). Own NCE NRC-2694-A (oral TKI) in a US/India Phase 2 in head-and-neck cancer. Carrying values: eGenesis Rs72.5 cr, Stero Rs9.6 cr, Cellogen Rs17.7 cr (AR FY26 note 7).

capital.buyback: 3.45 mn shares bought back in FY23-FY24 (87,050 in FY23, 3,360,245 in FY24); none since
capital.dividends: Rs6.0 a share paid in FY25, Rs5.0 in FY26 (interims), Rs1.5 for Q1FY27
capital.rights: Board finalised a rights issue on 25-Sep-2026: 17,058,082 shares at Rs750 (2 for 21), Rs1,279.36 cr; record date 1-Oct-2026 (30-Sep-2026 was the last cum-rights day); up to Rs810.5 cr to repay loans (SBI term loan Rs300 cr, IndusInd overdraft Rs200 cr, Bajaj Finance Rs310.5 cr), Rs110 cr R&D, rest general corporate purposes and inorganic growth
capital.buybackStance: CEO, 29-May-2026, on a buyback: 'No... this cash should be used for an acquisition'

management.text: V.C. Nannapaneni (founder, Chairman & MD since 1981); Rajeev Nannapaneni (Vice Chairman & CEO, on the board since 2005); Amit Parekh CFO from 13-Feb-2026 (S.V.V.N. Appa Rao retired); Rajesh Chebiyam EVP Crop Health. FY26 pay: VCN Rs7.60 cr, Rajeev Rs7.39 cr (both -24%), ~1% of PAT. Five independent directors; lead independent director D. Vijaya Bhaskar. Resolutions to re-appoint both for further terms were put to the 30-Sep-2026 AGM (AR FY26 notice).

accounting.exceptional: Screener's exceptional row is small (FY23 +Rs14 cr, FY24 -Rs2 cr, FY25 +Rs2 cr, FY26 -Rs18 cr after tax). One-offs not in that row: FY25 Rs90.1 cr gain on sale of land/PPE (other income); FY26 Rs115 cr one-time deferred-tax credit (new tax regime), 8% of FY26 PAT; Q4FY26 Rs20-30 cr engineering-spares write-down; FY26 litigation provisions Rs55.9 cr.
accounting.refundLiability: Refund liability (price protection and expected returns) Rs494.5 cr at Mar-26 vs Rs16.8 cr at Mar-25 (AR FY26 note 19e): mostly lenalidomide price protection after full generic entry; settles in FY27.
accounting.unbilled: Unbilled revenue (profit share accrued) Rs150.7 cr at Mar-26 vs Rs833.8 cr at Mar-25.

Generic sofosbuvir (India); Tamiflu FTF; generic Copaxone in the US
gRevlimid launch in the US (Mar-2022); CTPR in India
Open-market buyback (3.45 mn shares); Kothur warning letter (Apr-2024); eGenesis and Cellogen stakes
Kothur warning letter closed (Sep-2025); 35.75% of Adcock Ingram (Nov-2025)

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Natco Pharma (consolidated, Ind AS, Rs crore; Screener basis: revenue from operations, EBITDA before other income). One revenue path (sum of the business-line build in `businessLines`, checked in tools/authoring/NATCOPHARM.ctx.js) and one EBITDA margin. The 49% associate Adcock Ingram (South Africa, delisted from the JSE in Nov-2025, equity-accounted) has no engine line: Natco's share of its profit is carried in `otherIncome` (pre-tax) and the tax rate is set so tax falls only on profit before the associate share (`taxBuild`). Other income is built in `otherIncomeBuild` from sourced parts. Shares: 179.11 mn in issue (NATCOPHARM.patch.js). The Sep-2026 rights issue (Rs1,279 cr at Rs750, record date 1-Oct-2026) is NOT in the base: the 30-Sep-2026 close is cum-rights and the engine cannot change the share count; a post-rights view is shown in the valuation chapter. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build (`businessLines`). FY26 revenue from operations Rs4,078.3 cr (AR FY26 consolidated P&L): export formulations Rs3,234.5 cr (US Rs2,381.0 cr, Brazil Rs287.5 cr, Canada Rs251.7 cr, rest of world Rs314.3 cr by difference), domestic formulations Rs440.9 cr, API Rs234.7 cr, Crop Health Sciences Rs138.2 cr, other operating revenue Rs30.0 cr (Q1FY27 investor presentation; AR FY26 MD&A). FY27E Rs3,000 cr (-26%): no lenalidomide (Q1FY27 'negligible'); Q1FY27 revenue Rs735 cr is the run-rate (Rs2,940 cr annualised) and we add a modest H2 lift from Brazil (US$55-60 mn guided), CHS's kharif quarter and US approvals. Management guided 'gross sales' of Rs3,300-3,400 cr (14-Aug-2026 call; Rs3,400-3,500 cr total revenue in May): we are ~10% below because the guidance needs a ~20% jump over Q1 for the rest of the year. FY28E +16.7%: two US launches with exclusivity guided for FY28 (unnamed; carfilzomib's settlement launch is in CY2027), Brazil and Canada launches, domestic +13%. FY29E +11.3%.
assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (revenue from operations less operating costs; other income excluded). History: 14% FY22 (pre-gRevlimid), 35% FY23, 44% FY24, 50% FY25, 36% FY26 (24.6% in Q3FY26 and 17.3% in Q4FY26 with 'literally no Revlimid'; Q4 carried a R&D spike and a Rs20-30 cr engineering-spares write-down), 25.3% in Q1FY27 (low R&D quarter; management: 'there will be a little bit higher spend going forward'). FY27E 25.0%: Q1 level held (R&D 7-9% of sales guided vs 10.5% in FY26 offsets higher spend later in the year). FY28E 27.0%: limited-competition US launches carry high margins; FY29E 27.5%. We do not assume the 44-50% of the gRevlimid years.
assumptions._capexWhy: CFO Amit Parekh (14-Aug-2026): 'Organically, I think every year, we have around INR 250 crores to INR 300 crores of capex'. FY26 purchase of PPE Rs388 cr, FY25 Rs401 cr (AR FY26 cash flow). We use the top of the range: Rs300 cr a year. Acquisitions (Adcock tranche, July 2026) are handled in `otherIncomeBuild`, not capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation, amortisation and impairment Rs206.6 cr = 5.0% of average gross block (Screener Rs4,016 cr / Rs4,256 cr); Q1FY27 Rs47.1 cr (Rs188 cr annualised, 4.4% of the Mar-26 gross block). 4.4% on the growing block gives ~Rs194 / 207 / 220 cr. CWIP (Rs294 cr) held flat by the engine.

otherTreasury._why: Deposits with financial institutions (other than banks) inside Screener's 'other assets': Rs663.6 cr current + Rs40.0 cr non-current (AR FY26 consolidated note 9). With cash and bank balances Rs1,551 cr, investments Rs3,127 cr (of which Rs2,275.7 cr is the equity-accounted Adcock stake, note 41) and borrowings Rs714 cr (incl. leases), the engine's opening treasury is Rs4,668 cr, i.e. ~Rs2,392 cr of net cash plus the Adcock stake at book (management: 'net cash would be around INR 2,400 crores at a group level', 29-May-2026).

assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 interest income Rs231.5 cr (AR FY26 note 23) on average gross cash and deposits of roughly Rs3,500 cr before the Nov-2025 Adcock payment (6.5-7%). We use 6.5%. The engine applies it to its opening treasury, which includes the non-yielding Adcock stake; `otherIncomeBuild` removes that yield and adds the yield on cash funded by borrowings.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in `otherIncomeBuild`: Natco's share of Adcock Ingram's profit (Rs218 / 215 / 235 cr) + forex gains Rs25 cr a year (FY26 Rs39.1 cr, FY25 Rs19.8 cr) + recurring miscellaneous income Rs25 cr (FY26 misc Rs20.6 cr + wind power Rs3.5 cr + investment gains Rs2.4 cr) + 6.5% on the cash funded by ~Rs1,000 cr of borrowings (Rs65 cr) - 6.5% on the non-yielding Adcock stake inside the engine's treasury (Rs3,336 cr at the start of FY27, growing with half of Natco's share of Adcock's profit, which we assume is retained). FY27E other income including the associate: ~Rs420 cr (treasury ~Rs152 cr) vs FY26 Rs297.6 cr + associate Rs46.6 cr; no land-sale gains (FY25 Rs90.1 cr) are forecast.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (term loans, overdraft and short-term borrowings)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs36.7 cr on borrowings of Rs706 cr at Mar-26 (Rs400 cr term loan drawn in FY26); Q1FY27 Rs13.0 cr. The July-2026 Adcock tranche (Rs1,060 cr) was part-funded with debt: the rights-issue terms (25-Sep-2026) name Rs810.5 cr of loans to repay (SBI term loan Rs300 cr, IndusInd overdraft Rs200 cr, Bajaj Finance Rs310.5 cr). We hold gross borrowings at ~Rs1,000 cr (no rights issue in the base) at ~6.5%: Rs60 / 65 / 65 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on profit before the associate share (engine has no associate line). Built in `taxBuild`: 28% / 27% / 27% of PBT excluding the Adcock share (new regime from FY27: 25.17% statutory; CFO: 'roughly in India will be around 27%' with CSR disallowances; Brazil above 35%; Q1FY27 34%). The engine rate = that tax / PBT including the associate share. Checked each year in NATCOPHARM.ctx.js. FY26's 8% effective rate included a one-time Rs115 cr deferred-tax credit on moving to the new regime.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Quarterly interim dividends: Rs5.0 a share paid in FY26 (Rs2.0 + 1.5 + 1.5; Rs89.6 cr), Rs6.0 in FY25; Rs1.50 declared for Q1FY27 (14-Aug-2026). 15% of our EPS is ~Rs6-8 a share. No buyback planned: CEO on 29-May-2026, asked about a buyback, 'No... this cash should be used for an acquisition'.

businessLines._note: Revenue from operations by business line (Rs crore). FY26 from the Q1FY27 investor presentation (segment table) and AR FY26 MD&A (US, Brazil, Canada); rest of world by difference. Checked against model revenue in NATCOPHARM.ctx.js (tolerance 0.5%).
businessLines._why: US: Q1FY27 export formulations Rs477 cr less Brazil Rs178 cr and Canada Rs56 cr leaves ~Rs243 cr a quarter for the US and other markets with negligible lenalidomide; US ~Rs165 cr a quarter, plus H2 approvals ('two US orders'; eribulin approved in Q1) gives Rs860 cr for FY27E; FY28E Rs1,080 cr with the two exclusivity launches management guides for FY28 (we assume ~Rs200 cr in the first year), FY29E Rs1,200 cr. Brazil: FY26 Rs287.5 cr; 'should go to US$55-60 million this year' (29-May-2026); Q1FY27 Rs178 cr (+180%): Rs530 / 620 / 700 cr. Canada: FY26 Rs251.7 cr (AR; Rs229 cr for the subsidiary on the call), 'grow around 10% to 15%', big launches in FY28: Rs270 / 310 / 345 cr. Rest of world (MENA tenders, Asia, China): +10% / +9% / +8%. Domestic: FY26 Rs440.9 cr; Q1FY27 Rs136 cr (+27%), semaglutide ~Rs2 cr a month own brand plus partners, 'domestic will increase by about 25% in volumes': +22% / +13% / +12%. API: FY26 Rs234.7 cr, Q1 Rs66.7 cr: Rs260 / 280 / 300 cr. CHS: FY26 Rs138.2 cr (FY25 Rs59.8 cr), Q1 Rs40.8 cr, breakeven targeted for FY27; demerger planned by ~Mar-2027 (kept in the base: it is near breakeven and shareholders keep the value): Rs165 / 195 / 230 cr.

otherIncomeBuild._note: Engine other income = 6.5% x opening engine treasury (treasuryYield) + otherIncome; otherIncome = associate + forex + misc + carry - yield on non-yielding stake (Rs crore).
otherIncomeBuild._why: Non-yielding stake: Adcock carrying value Rs2,275.7 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 41) + the 13.25% tranche bought in July 2026 for ZAR1.81 bn (~Rs1,060 cr; CEO 14-Aug-2026), both still inside the engine's treasury because the engine cannot book an acquisition; it grows each year by half of Natco's share of Adcock's profit (we assume half is paid out as dividends; FY26 dividend received Rs36.9 cr). Adcock profit (100%): Q1FY27 Rs242.2 cr (flu season), 'normally the profit is usually around INR 100 crores per quarter' (CFO, 14-Aug-2026): FY27E Rs542 cr; Natco's share = Q1 Rs84.3 cr actual + Q2 at a blended 44.6% + Q3-Q4 at 49% - ~Rs3 cr a quarter of purchase-price amortisation = Rs218 cr. FY28E Adcock Rs470 cr (normal year, May-2026 guidance US$47-48 mn PAT), FY29E Rs510 cr: 49% less ~Rs15 cr amortisation = Rs215 / 235 cr. Carry: 6.5% on ~Rs1,000 cr of gross borrowings, which the engine nets against cash.

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = tax at taxOnPbtExAssoc% on (PBT - associate share) / PBT.
taxBuild._why: New tax regime from FY27 (25.17% statutory); India effective ~27% with disallowances (CFO, 14-Aug-2026); Brazil above 35%; Q1FY27 34% on a large Brazil share. 28% for FY27E, 27% thereafter.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, so the cost of equity is the discount rate. Natco's earnings are lumpy (exclusivity windows, litigation outcomes): beta 0.9 gives 11.9%, above DRREDDY's 11.6%.
dcf._tgWhy: House range 5-6%; we use 5.0% because a third of the business is US limited-competition generics whose profits decay after each launch.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Screener-basis EBITDA margin fades from 27.5% to 26%: exclusivity launches recur but each erodes; the branded and Brazil base runs at mid-20s.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex moves from ~8% of revenue (FY29E; FY23-FY26 ran at 8-10%) to 6% in the long run: maintenance plus new lines for a business several times today's size.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The FY28 US exclusivities (carfilzomib and a second unnamed product) launch on time with few competitors; olaparib wins at trial; Brazil keeps doubling; Adcock earns US$55 mn+ a year; EBITDA margin returns to ~30%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: US launches slip or face many generics; Brazil tenders fall back; semaglutide stays a price war in India; Adcock's rand profits disappoint; a new USFDA problem at Kothur or Vizag; margins stuck near 22%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Natco: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (ICICI Securities, 31-May-2026: 18x FY28E core EPS plus an NPV of Rs100 a share for exclusive products; the other brokers we could read do not disclose a method). Our multiple: Natco's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on reported EPS (house forwardMedian; trough years FY27 and FY28 excluded by the rule) x the pharma sector factor for names outside the nine-peer set (+8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c), nearest half-turn; bull = 75th percentile x factor, bear = 25th percentile x factor. Written by tools/authoring/NATCOPHARM.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (trough rule applied to forward EBITDA) x the nine peers' EV/EBITDA factor (+7.5%), nearest half-turn; plus the engine's treasury at Sep-28E (net cash and the Adcock stake at book). NATCOPHARM.ctx.js.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: 15-year FCFF at the 11.9% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.0%, plus the engine's treasury at Mar-27 (net cash and the Adcock stake at book).

cover.headline: gRevlimid is over; what is left earns ₹40-55 a share, and on the house multiple that is worth less than the price
cover.lead: Natco Pharma is a Hyderabad generics company that lives on hard-to-copy US generics. Its biggest one, generic Revlimid (lenalidomide), sold under a volume-limited licence from Mar-2022 to Jan-2026 and lifted EPS from ₹9 (FY22) to ₹104 (FY25); we estimate ~₹6,900 cr of lenalidomide revenue over FY23-FY26. That windfall is gone: Q1FY27 EPS was ₹11.5 and 41% of the profit came from Adcock Ingram, the South African company Natco now owns 49% of. The street values Natco on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (ICICI Securities: 18x FY28E core EPS plus ₹100 a share for exclusive products). We forecast EPS of ₹40.2 / ₹48.7 / ₹55.4 for FY27-29E. Natco's own forward P/E since Apr-2021 has a median of **10.4x** once the rule drops the trough years (FY27 and FY28: forward EPS below half the FY25 peak), because what remains are the windfall years when the market paid 7-8x for gRevlimid profits. Times the pharma factor (+8.2%) that gives **11.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹52.0 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**. **We initiate with SELL.** We flag plainly that the cross-checks are far higher (EV/EBITDA ₹917, DCF ₹897) and that the since-2021 median with no years dropped would give ₹990. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The windfall has ended, and it was most of the profit
arguments.p: Export formulations were ₹1,127 cr in Q1FY26 and ₹421 cr in Q3FY26, the first quarter with "0 Revlimid". EBITDA margin (before other income) went from 50% in FY25 to 25% in Q1FY27. We estimate gRevlimid added ~₹4,300 cr of EBITDA over FY23-FY26; FY27E profit (~₹720 cr) is about half of FY26's.

arguments.h: What is left: a ₹3,000 cr business plus 49% of Adcock
arguments.p: Brazil (+180% in Q1), India (+27%, semaglutide), Canada and the US base make ~₹3,000 cr of revenue at a mid-20s margin. Adcock adds ₹218 cr of profit in FY27E, 30.3% of our PAT, from a company Natco does not control. Management guides ~₹750 cr of FY27 profit and 15-25% growth a year from FY28; we are slightly below on both.

arguments.h: The pipeline is real but unnamed and lumpy
arguments.p: Carfilzomib (sole FTF on one strength, settlement launch expected in CY2027), two FY28 US exclusivities management will not name, olaparib still in court, semaglutide in the US years away. Natco filed no major new first-to-file in FY26. The CEO calls it "a roller coaster"; we agree.

arguments.h: Valuation: the house rule says expensive; the street and our cross-checks disagree
arguments.p: At ₹828 the stock trades at 17.0x our FY28E EPS and 15.9x Sep-28E. The street (post-Q4 notes, median ₹1,058) pays ~18x core earnings. Our 11.5x comes from the rule as written; on a since-2021 median with no trough years dropped (19x) the target would be ₹990. The rating hangs on that multiple.

catalysts: Rights issue: record date 1-Oct-2026 (30-Sep-2026 was the last cum-rights day); ₹1,279 cr at ₹750, 2 for 21, mostly to repay ₹810.5 cr of loans.
Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first full quarter at 49% of Adcock and the test of the ₹3,300-3,400 cr sales guidance.
US launches: carfilzomib (settlement date confidential; CY2027 expected) and the two FY28 exclusivities; the olaparib patent trial ("in the next few months").
Crop Health Sciences demerger (moved from Dec-2026 to ~Mar-2027) and the USFDA inspection of the Visakhapatnam plant (due).
A second large acquisition (management: one outside India, one smaller in India); eGenesis kidney-xenotransplant registration trial from early 2027.

sections.title: What Natco does: picks fights over patents, sells the winners through partners, and has branched into India, Brazil, South Africa and pesticides

blocks.p: Natco Pharma was founded in Hyderabad in 1981 by V.C. Nannapaneni, who still chairs it; his son Rajeev is Vice Chairman and CEO. It is a **niche generics** company: it looks for medicines that are hard to make or legally risky to copy, challenges the patents (a "para-IV" filing in the US), and, if it wins or settles, sells the generic with few competitors for a while. In the US it mostly works with partners (Teva, Mylan/Viatris, Breckenridge, Lupin, Dr. Reddy's, Sun) who market the drug and share litigation costs; Natco makes the product and takes a **profit share**. Total revenue was ₹4,376 cr in FY26 (revenue from operations ₹4,078 cr) and profit ₹1,419 cr.

blocks.p: Two things follow. First, Natco's profit has always been **lumpy**: a few exclusivity products (Copaxone and Tamiflu generics in 2016-18, Revlimid in 2022-26) made most of the money for a few years each. Second, the base underneath (India, Brazil, Canada, APIs, a US front end) is small: domestic formulations were ₹441 cr in FY26 against ₹477 cr in FY22. Management's stated aim is to flip the mix so the base makes ~70% of profit and first-to-file products 25-30%; "earlier, the ratio was the other way around" (CEO, 29-May-2026).

blocks.callout: **So what:** an investor in Natco buys a portfolio of patent bets plus a modest branded base, with ~30.3% of FY27E profit coming from a South African company it does not control. Value depends on how many bets pay off and how management spends the cash in between.

blocks.p: The corporate actions that matter for today's numbers: (1) the Dec-2015 Revlimid settlement gave Natco a volume-limited US licence from Mar-2022 and full entry from 31-Jan-2026, which is the whole FY23-FY26 hump; (2) the FY23-FY24 open-market buyback of 3.45 mn shares took the count to 179.11 mn, unchanged since; (3) Adcock Ingram, 35.75% in Nov-2025 and 49% from Jul-2026, equity-accounted; (4) the board-approved demerger of Crop Health Sciences (pending approvals; ~Mar-2027); (5) the rights issue set on 25-Sep-2026 (₹750 a share, 2 for 21, record date 1-Oct-2026), which will lift the share count to ~196.2 mn in Oct-2026.

blocks.callout: **Track record of the big bets:** Revlimid paid off hugely; the Tamiflu and Copaxone generics (2016-17) lifted EPS from ₹9 (FY16) to ₹37 (FY18) before it faded to ₹25 (FY20); the hepatitis-C launches (sofosbuvir, 2015) lifted the India business, which then shrank from ₹540 cr (FY20) to ₹375 cr (FY23); Crop Health has taken six years to reach ₹138 cr of sales and still loses money in some quarters. The pattern is a few large wins, several small ones and long gaps.

sections.title: Industry: US first-to-file windfalls are getting rarer; emerging markets and Indian GLP-1s are crowded but growing

blocks.p: **US generics.** US generics is a 'winner takes all' market for first-to-file (FTF) para-IV products: the first filer can get 180 days of exclusivity; after that, prices fall 80-90% as more generics enter. Natco's model is to pick hard-to-make or litigated molecules with few filers and partner with a US marketer (Teva, Mylan/Viatris, Breckenridge, Lupin, Dr. Reddy's, Sun, Alvogen) who shares litigation cost and pays a profit share. CEO (29-May-2026): 'especially if you're doing an NCE-1, chances are most products, you have 8 or 10 or 15 or 20 guys who file on day'; 'if we're able to pull off in a 3 to 4 year time period... even 3 of those, you have done a great job'. FY26: 7-8 US filings, no major FTF.

**India.** Semaglutide went off patent in India in Mar-2026; Natco launched the first generic vial on day one and the pen a month later; 10-15 generics; CEO: 'The market is cutthroat'; own brand ~Rs2 cr a month; vial < Rs1,000 a month vs pen Rs3,000-4,000. Natco's own India business is small (₹441 cr, FY26) and was flat for years before semaglutide.

**Emerging markets.** Brazil, Canada and South Africa are markets where generics are sold under company brands or via tenders; registration takes 18-24 months, so new entrants need years or an acquisition. Adcock Ingram is the second-largest South African pharma company by private-market share; four divisions (prescription, OTC, hospital, consumer); three plants near Johannesburg and 49% of an Indian JV with two plants.
**Crop protection.** Indian crop-protection market ~US$2.6-2.7 bn (2025-26), projected US$3.36 bn by 2031 (4.45% CAGR); input costs rose 25-30% after the West Asia war (Natco CHS head, 29-May-2026).

bullets: **GLP-1 genericisation:** semaglutide is off patent in India (Mar-2026) and in more emerging markets in 2026-27; in the US, Natco is a sole first-to-file on some strengths of Ozempic and Wegovy (partner Mylan/Viatris), though launch is years away.
**Weaker rupee:** most of Natco's revenue is earned in dollars, reais, Canadian dollars and (via Adcock) rand.
**Fewer windfalls:** most new US filings now face 8-20 day-one filers; Natco made no major new first-to-file in FY26.
**Price wars in India:** 10-15 semaglutide generics; Natco's own brand sells ~₹2 cr a month and "doesn't make much money".
**Regulation and tariffs:** US tariff talk on generics and USFDA inspections (Visakhapatnam due); input costs up 25-30% for agrochemicals after the West Asia war.

sections.title: gRevlimid: ~₹6,900 cr of revenue and ~₹4,300 cr of extra EBITDA in four years, and now almost nothing

blocks.p: In Dec-2015 Celgene (now BMS) settled the Revlimid (lenalidomide) patent case with Natco, its US partner Arrow International and Arrow's parent Watson (Actavis generics, now part of Teva): Natco got a volume-limited licence from Mar-2022 (expected to reach a mid-single-digit percentage of US capsules in the final year) and unlimited generic entry from 31-Jan-2026 (patents expire Apr-2027). Natco books a profit share on its partner's sales. Quotas reset each January and were sold early in the year: Q3FY25 and Q3FY26 export formulations fell to Rs286 cr and Rs421 cr ('We had 0 Revlimid this quarter', 12-Feb-2026). From Feb-2026 the product is a crowded generic: Q1FY27 lenalidomide was 'negligible'. Canada: Natco has the 'highest market share for Lenalidomide'.

Natco does not disclose lenalidomide sales, so we estimate them. Two quarters tell us what the business looks like without the product: Q3FY25 (export formulations ₹286 cr) and Q3FY26 (₹421 cr, "0 Revlimid"). Everything above that run-rate in a year is, roughly, lenalidomide. The US revenue the annual reports disclose moves the same way: ₹1,606 cr (FY23), ₹2,805 cr (FY24), ₹3,149 cr (FY25), ₹2,381 cr (FY26).

sections.title: The base business: Brazil is the star, India gets a semaglutide lift, Canada is steady; together ~₹1,900 cr growing mid-teens

blocks.p: **India (domestic formulations).** ₹441 cr in FY26, +10.2%; ₹136 cr in Q1FY27 (+27%; the base runs ~₹107 cr a quarter, semaglutide and third-party orders did the rest). Natco is a pioneer in branded cancer generics in India (top 3 in the segments it operates in; 10 brands above ₹10 cr), plus hepatology (Velpanat), cardiology (Apigat close to #2 in prescriptions) and diabetology. It launched the first generic semaglutide vial in Mar-2026; the brand sells ~₹2 cr a month and, with partners Eris and Glenmark, adds ~₹4 cr a month to sales. The CEO: "As of now, it doesn't lose money, but it doesn't make much money either." We model +22% / +13% / +12%.

**Brazil.** ₹288 cr in FY26 and ₹178 cr in Q1FY27 alone (+180%), from oncology launches (carfilzomib, eltrombopag, apixaban) and being the single source of everolimus in Brazil for the fourth year running. Management guided US$55-60 mn for FY27; we use ₹530 cr, then ₹620 / 700 cr. Brazil sales are tender-driven, so quarters swing; tax there is above 35%.

**Canada.** ₹252 cr in FY26 (the subsidiary alone ₹229 cr); a top-10 generic company in Canada with the highest market share in lenalidomide and oseltamivir; ₹56 cr in Q1FY27. Guided +10-15%, with "a couple of big launches" in FY28. We model ₹270 / 310 / 345 cr. **Rest of world** (MENA tenders in Saudi Arabia, Algeria, Egypt; Asia; first launches in China): ~₹314 cr in FY26 by difference; we grow it 8-10% a year.

blocks.p: Is it a good deal? On cost, Natco paid ~₹3,140 cr for a profit share we put at ₹215-235 cr a year from FY28E: about 14x earnings, or a ~7% return, which the CEO himself called "only slightly better than bank interest" (29-May-2026). blocks.p: **Chlorantraniliprole (CTPR)** is a broad-spectrum insecticide. Natco launched CTPR products in India in 2022 using the same techno-legal approach as in pharma, and CHS sales jumped to ₹108 cr in FY24, then fell to ₹60 cr in FY25 (the CHS head calls those years "mostly learning in terms of how the market works"). The recovery to ₹138 cr in FY26 came from new products (the fungicide Glanz, cyantraniliprole) and more distributors: CTPR is now only ~30-35% of CHS sales. Q1FY27 (₹41 cr) still made an EBITDA loss because rains came late; the second quarter (kharif) is the biggest. Raw materials rose 25-30% after the West Asia war.

The demerger (shareholders get shares in Natco Crop Health Sciences Ltd; timing moved to ~Mar-2027) is value-neutral for a Natco shareholder; we keep CHS in the consolidated forecasts until it happens and do not assign it a separate value.

sections.title: Four windfall years: revenue doubled and profit rose 4x on gRevlimid; FY27 falls back to about the FY23 level

blocks.p: Natco's numbers only make sense once you split out generic Revlimid (lenalidomide). Revenue went from ₹1,945 cr in FY22 to a peak of ₹4,430 cr in FY25, and EBITDA (Screener basis: before other income) from ₹264 cr to ₹2,196 cr, a 50% margin. EPS went from ₹9.2 to ₹104.4. Profit after tax was ₹5,404 cr over FY23-FY26, 2.4x the ₹2,237 cr of FY18-FY21. The base business underneath grew far more slowly. In FY26 the volume-limited period ended (unlimited generic entry from 31-Jan-2026): revenue fell 8% and EPS to ₹79.2, flattered by a ₹115 cr one-time tax credit. Q1FY27 EPS was ₹11.5, with almost no lenalidomide and 41% of profit coming from the new South African associate, Adcock Ingram.

sections.title: Margins: 50% was the windfall; the business without it earns about 25% before other income

blocks.p: Natco reports "EBITDA including other income" (39.6% in FY26, 30.9% in Q1FY27). We use Screener's basis, which excludes other income: 49.6% in FY25, 35.9% in FY26, 25.3% in Q1FY27. The gap matters at Natco because other income (interest on ~₹2,000-3,000 cr of cash, forex, licensing) is large. Gross margin is unusually high because profit-share revenue carries no material cost: materials were 15.6% of revenue in FY25 and 16.9% in FY26. blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Natco generated ₹5,871 cr of operating cash flow, spent ₹1,966 cr on fixed assets and paid ₹665 cr of dividends. It bought back 3.45 mn shares in FY23-FY24 (open market). The big use of the windfall came at the end: ₹2,079 cr (ZAR3,873 mn plus ₹88 cr of costs) for 35.75% of Adcock Ingram in Nov-2025, and ~₹1,060 cr (ZAR1.81 bn) for another 13.25% in July 2026. On 25-Sep-2026 the board set a ₹1,279 cr rights issue at ₹750 a share, mainly to repay ₹810.5 cr of those loans. Management has said no to buybacks and wants "another very large transaction".

New shares offered to existing holders in proportion to holdings (2 for 21 at ₹750). TERP = theoretical price after the issue.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Natco Pharma (consolidated, Ind AS, Rs crore; Screener basis: revenue from operations, EBITDA before other income). One revenue path (sum of the business-line build in `businessLines`, checked in tools/authoring/NATCOPHARM.ctx.js) and one EBITDA margin. The 49% associate Adcock Ingram (South Africa, delisted from the JSE in Nov-2025, equity-accounted) has no engine line: Natco's share of its profit is carried in `otherIncome` (pre-tax) and the tax rate is set so tax falls only on profit before the associate share (`taxBuild`). Other income is built in `otherIncomeBuild` from sourced parts. Shares: 179.11 mn in issue (NATCOPHARM.patch.js). The Sep-2026 rights issue (Rs1,279 cr at Rs750, record date 1-Oct-2026) is NOT in the base: the 30-Sep-2026 close is cum-rights and the engine cannot change the share count; a post-rights view is shown in the valuation chapter. assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build (`businessLines`). FY26 revenue from operations Rs4,078.3 cr (AR FY26 consolidated P&L): export formulations Rs3,234.5 cr (US Rs2,381.0 cr, Brazil Rs287.5 cr, Canada Rs251.7 cr, rest of world Rs314.3 cr by difference), domestic formulations Rs440.9 cr, API Rs234.7 cr, Crop Health Sciences Rs138.2 cr, other operating revenue Rs30.0 cr (Q1FY27 investor presentation; AR FY26 MD&A). FY27E Rs3,000 cr (-26%): no lenalidomide (Q1FY27 'negligible'); Q1FY27 revenue Rs735 cr is the run-rate (Rs2,940 cr annualised) and we add a modest H2 lift from Brazil (US$55-60 mn guided), CHS's kharif quarter and US approvals. Management guided 'gross sales' of Rs3,300-3,400 cr (14-Aug-2026 call; Rs3,400-3,500 cr total revenue in May): we are ~10% below because the guidance needs a ~20% jump over Q1 for the rest of the year. FY28E +16.7%: two US launches with exclusivity guided for FY28 (unnamed; carfilzomib's settlement launch is in CY2027), Brazil and Canada launches, domestic +13%. FY29E +11.3%.
assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (revenue from operations less operating costs; other income excluded). History: 14% FY22 (pre-gRevlimid), 35% FY23, 44% FY24, 50% FY25, 36% FY26 (24.6% in Q3FY26 and 17.3% in Q4FY26 with 'literally no Revlimid'; Q4 carried a R&D spike and a Rs20-30 cr engineering-spares write-down), 25.3% in Q1FY27 (low R&D quarter; management: 'there will be a little bit higher spend going forward'). FY27E 25.0%: Q1 level held (R&D 7-9% of sales guided vs 10.5% in FY26 offsets higher spend later in the year). FY28E 27.0%: limited-competition US launches carry high margins; FY29E 27.5%. We do not assume the 44-50% of the gRevlimid years.
assumptions._capexWhy: CFO Amit Parekh (14-Aug-2026): 'Organically, I think every year, we have around INR 250 crores to INR 300 crores of capex'. FY26 purchase of PPE Rs388 cr, FY25 Rs401 cr (AR FY26 cash flow). We use the top of the range: Rs300 cr a year. Acquisitions (Adcock tranche, July 2026) are handled in `otherIncomeBuild`, not capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation, amortisation and impairment Rs206.6 cr = 5.0% of average gross block (Screener Rs4,016 cr / Rs4,256 cr); Q1FY27 Rs47.1 cr (Rs188 cr annualised, 4.4% of the Mar-26 gross block). 4.4% on the growing block gives ~Rs194 / 207 / 220 cr. CWIP (Rs294 cr) held flat by the engine.

otherTreasury._why: Deposits with financial institutions (other than banks) inside Screener's 'other assets': Rs663.6 cr current + Rs40.0 cr non-current (AR FY26 consolidated note 9). With cash and bank balances Rs1,551 cr, investments Rs3,127 cr (of which Rs2,275.7 cr is the equity-accounted Adcock stake, note 41) and borrowings Rs714 cr (incl. leases), the engine's opening treasury is Rs4,668 cr, i.e. ~Rs2,392 cr of net cash plus the Adcock stake at book (management: 'net cash would be around INR 2,400 crores at a group level', 29-May-2026).

assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 interest income Rs231.5 cr (AR FY26 note 23) on average gross cash and deposits of roughly Rs3,500 cr before the Nov-2025 Adcock payment (6.5-7%). We use 6.5%. The engine applies it to its opening treasury, which includes the non-yielding Adcock stake; `otherIncomeBuild` removes that yield and adds the yield on cash funded by borrowings.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in `otherIncomeBuild`: Natco's share of Adcock Ingram's profit (Rs218 / 215 / 235 cr) + forex gains Rs25 cr a year (FY26 Rs39.1 cr, FY25 Rs19.8 cr) + recurring miscellaneous income Rs25 cr (FY26 misc Rs20.6 cr + wind power Rs3.5 cr + investment gains Rs2.4 cr) + 6.5% on the cash funded by ~Rs1,000 cr of borrowings (Rs65 cr) - 6.5% on the non-yielding Adcock stake inside the engine's treasury (Rs3,336 cr at the start of FY27, growing with half of Natco's share of Adcock's profit, which we assume is retained). FY27E other income including the associate: ~Rs420 cr (treasury ~Rs152 cr) vs FY26 Rs297.6 cr + associate Rs46.6 cr; no land-sale gains (FY25 Rs90.1 cr) are forecast.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (term loans, overdraft and short-term borrowings)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs36.7 cr on borrowings of Rs706 cr at Mar-26 (Rs400 cr term loan drawn in FY26); Q1FY27 Rs13.0 cr. The July-2026 Adcock tranche (Rs1,060 cr) was part-funded with debt: the rights-issue terms (25-Sep-2026) name Rs810.5 cr of loans to repay (SBI term loan Rs300 cr, IndusInd overdraft Rs200 cr, Bajaj Finance Rs310.5 cr). assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on profit before the associate share (engine has no associate line). Built in `taxBuild`: 28% / 27% / 27% of PBT excluding the Adcock share (new regime from FY27: 25.17% statutory; CFO: 'roughly in India will be around 27%' with CSR disallowances; Brazil above 35%; Q1FY27 34%). assumptions._payoutWhy: Quarterly interim dividends: Rs5.0 a share paid in FY26 (Rs2.0 + 1.5 + 1.5; Rs89.6 cr), Rs6.0 in FY25; Rs1.50 declared for Q1FY27 (14-Aug-2026). 15% of our EPS is ~Rs6-8 a share. businessLines._note: Revenue from operations by business line (Rs crore). FY26 from the Q1FY27 investor presentation (segment table) and AR FY26 MD&A (US, Brazil, Canada); rest of world by difference. Checked against model revenue in NATCOPHARM.ctx.js (tolerance 0.5%).
businessLines._why: US: Q1FY27 export formulations Rs477 cr less Brazil Rs178 cr and Canada Rs56 cr leaves ~Rs243 cr a quarter for the US and other markets with negligible lenalidomide; US ~Rs165 cr a quarter, plus H2 approvals ('two US orders'; eribulin approved in Q1) gives Rs860 cr for FY27E; FY28E Rs1,080 cr with the two exclusivity launches management guides for FY28 (we assume ~Rs200 cr in the first year), FY29E Rs1,200 cr. Canada: FY26 Rs251.7 cr (AR; Rs229 cr for the subsidiary on the call), 'grow around 10% to 15%', big launches in FY28: Rs270 / 310 / 345 cr. Rest of world (MENA tenders, Asia, China): +10% / +9% / +8%. Domestic: FY26 Rs440.9 cr; Q1FY27 Rs136 cr (+27%), semaglutide ~Rs2 cr a month own brand plus partners, 'domestic will increase by about 25% in volumes': +22% / +13% / +12%. API: FY26 Rs234.7 cr, Q1 Rs66.7 cr: Rs260 / 280 / 300 cr. otherIncomeBuild._why: Non-yielding stake: Adcock carrying value Rs2,275.7 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 41) + the 13.25% tranche bought in July 2026 for ZAR1.81 bn (~Rs1,060 cr; CEO 14-Aug-2026), both still inside the engine's treasury because the engine cannot book an acquisition; it grows each year by half of Natco's share of Adcock's profit (we assume half is paid out as dividends; FY26 dividend received Rs36.9 cr). taxBuild._why: New tax regime from FY27 (25.17% statutory); India effective ~27% with disallowances (CFO, 14-Aug-2026); Brazil above 35%; Q1FY27 34% on a large Brazil share. 28% for FY27E, 27% thereafter.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, so the cost of equity is the discount rate. Natco's earnings are lumpy (exclusivity windows, litigation outcomes): beta 0.9 gives 11.9%, above DRREDDY's 11.6%.

dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Screener-basis EBITDA margin fades from 27.5% to 26%: exclusivity launches recur but each erodes; the branded and Brazil base runs at mid-20s.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex moves from ~8% of revenue (FY29E; FY23-FY26 ran at 8-10%) to 6% in the long run: maintenance plus new lines for a business several times today's size.

Our multiple: Natco's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on reported EPS (house forwardMedian; trough years FY27 and FY28 excluded by the rule) x the pharma sector factor for names outside the nine-peer set (+8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c), nearest half-turn; bull = 75th percentile x factor, bear = 25th percentile x factor.
